_about: Settings for Dubai's Routes page (engine/routes/: build.py, page.html), at /dubai/routes/: pick a bus or tram stop or Metro platform near you, see where each RTA route goes. The Metro comes from raw/surface/rapid_*.json (surface.json 'rapid'), its platforms in order. RTA publishes no open real-time feed, so every time on the page is from the timetable (surface.json 'sched'). Streets come from the map's own OpenStreetMap roads (tmp/streets_by_class.json, written by build.py).

page.title: Where does this bus, tram or Metro go?
page.description: Find the RTA bus and tram stops and Metro stations nearest you in Dubai and see where each route goes, with the next scheduled departures: the communities it passes through, the main roads it runs along, its Metro connections and the landmarks on the way.
page.lede: Find the stops and stations near you, then pick a bus, the tram or a Metro line to see where it goes: the communities, main roads, connections and landmarks along the way.
page.outside: That spot is too far from an RTA stop. Try a place in Dubai or near a Metro station.
page.noMatch: No match in Dubai for “{q}”. Try a community or landmark, like “Al Karama” or “Dubai Mall”.
page.noStops: No stops or stations within {r} of that spot.
page.credits: Routes, stops and timetable: RTA GTFS via Data Dubai (Dubai Open Data Licence) · Streets: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) · Times are scheduled: RTA publishes no open live feed
page.legendKnown: Dubai Marina: the names people use

badges._about: Route badge colours for apps: buses RTA's blue, the tram orange, Metro lines as plain dots in the line's colour.

_units: 'units' is route_areas (build.py): OpenStreetMap's communities, with the gaps between them (Dubai Marina, Al Barsha, Jebel Ali) named by the nearest known-as name, so a route's story doesn't carry the last community's name across a gap.
